{"id": "679921e9-d744-4ee6-a195-f49fc899949c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what's likely going on — Q Apps in Amazon Q Business has its own layer of gating that sits on top of regular chat access, so "IAM and Identity Center assignment check out" for chat doesn't mean they check out for Q Apps specifically. A few things to verify, in order of likelihood:

**1. Subscription tier — most common cause**
As of July 1, 2024, Q Apps is available **only to Amazon Q Business Pro subscribers**. Lite-tier users get a 403 when opening Q Apps even though regular chat works fine (chat is available on both tiers). Check the user's subscription tier in the Amazon Q Business console under Subscriptions — if they're on Lite, that's almost certainly it. Also note: Q Apps created by Lite users before the cutover may no longer be viewable/runnable even after the fact.

**2. IAM Identity Center assignment — assignment to the *app*, not just the user**
"IAM/Identity Center checks out" often means the user is assigned to the Q Business application and has a valid identity. But Q Apps authorization is derived separately from the user/group info IAM Identity Center passes through — if the user's group membership used for Q Apps' internal sharing/visibility permissions isn't synced or isn't present in the identity source, Q Apps-specific calls can be denied even though the base chat app assignment is fine. Worth double-checking group sync status in Identity Center, not just user assignment.

**3. IAM policy scope — `qapps:*` actions vs `qbusiness:*` actions**
Regular chat relies on `qbusiness:Chat`/`qbusiness:ChatSync`-type actions. Q Apps uses a distinct `qapps:*` action namespace (e.g., `qapps:CreateQApp`, `qapps:ListQApps`, `qapps:StartQAppSession`). If the user's/role's IAM policy was scoped to `qbusiness:*` only, chat will work but any Q Apps action returns 403 — this is a very common miss since admins often copy a chat-only policy.

**4. Feature not enabled at the application level**
Q Apps can be toggled on/off per Q Business application by the admin in application settings. If it's disabled org-wide, every user gets a 403 on Q Apps regardless of individual permissions — worth ruling out before digging into the specific user.

If you want, I can pull the actual Q Business application's subscription tier and the user's IAM policy document to confirm which of these it is — I'd need the application ID/account/region to look.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
